summary: Intro discovery to validate cost/unit economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer cares about per-token cost, tail latency under 150ms for 2k seq, batching and KV/prefix caching impacts, and security/KMS for private data. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing spreadsheet.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Marina Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Daniel Hart (Head of ML - Northwind), Priya Singh (Infra Lead - Northwind), Sanjay Rao (CFO - Northwind)

00:00 Marina (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
00:08 Daniel (Northwind): yeah hi i'm daniel, we run ml infra and models for the trading desk, been looking at LLMs for research summarization.
00:14 Priya (Northwind): priya here, infra and cloud lead, i'll own the benchmarking with you folks.
00:18 S anjay (Northwind): sanjay here, finance, i'll be listening for budget and procurement stuff.
00:22 Marina: great. ethan our se will walk through cost levers and how batching/caching affect unit economics, i'll handle pricing and commercial stuff.
00:30 Ethan (Redwood SE): thanks. small agenda: understand their workload, targets (latency, throughput), discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private cost profiles, and propose a pilot. sound good?
00:38 Daniel: yes. to start, typical requests are ~1.5k tokens input, we generate ~800 tokens on average, about 20k requests / day but bursty, qps may hit 30-40 during market open. latency target is sub 150ms p50 on generation tokens, p95 probably <450ms.
01:05 Ethan: ok that's helpful. some quick clarifying q's: is data residency or encryption a hard req? any compliance like SOC2?
01:12 Priya: SOC2 is required. data at rest / in transit must be customer KMS, and we need audit logs. we prefer VPC/private deployment if the cost delta isn't huge.
01:24 Marina: understood. sanjay, rough budget ballpark or procurement cadence?
01:28 Sanjay: we can pilot with ~20k/month for the first quarter but need clear unit economics before scaling. do you have an estimate per 1M tokens?
01:36 Marina: we do — i'll send a tailored sheet — but to set expectations: hosted is simpler and lower start-up cost but per-token is higher; dedicated brings unit cost down via reserved capacity; private has licensing and infra overhead. exact numbers depend on model, sequence length, batching and caching.
02:00 Ethan: on the technical side, a few levers strongly change per-token cost: batching (amortizes kernel work across concurrent requests), KV/prefix caching (avoids re-computing encoder prefixes for repeated prompts), sequence length — longer sequences cost more, and quantization/8-bit compiles reduce GPU memory and ops cost. also tail latency increases with batch size so there's a tradeoff.
02:28 Daniel: gives example: our current experiments show a 2x difference between single-request latency and batched latency at similar throughput. does redwood auto-batch?
02:35 Ethan: yes, the serving runtime supports continuous batching with configurable targets and latency SLOs. we also support adaptive batching so during bursts batch sizes grow but we cap to meet latency targets. small caveat, with 1.5k input + 800 output tokens you'll hit memory/KV cache sizing considerations.
03:02 Priya: how does KV cache help exactly? we do many repeated prefixes for internal summarization templates.
03:07 Ethan: KV/prefix cache stores the key/value tensors for tokens of the prefix so subsequent calls reuse them — that's huge for cost if you're repeating prompts. you can see up to 60-70% token compute savings for strict prefix reuse patterns. transcription: "K V cache" sometimes gets split in export.
03:28 Daniel: wow that's significant. how does that translate to per-token pricing in hosted?
03:31 Marina: hosted pricing has base per-input and per-output token tiers; with caching effective billed compute per token drops because the runtime doesn't execute full forward for cached tokens. so billed tokens depend on our metering — we meter generated tokens and non-cached encoder compute. i'll include a worked example in the sheet.
03:54 Sanjay: competitors like openai list per-token prices but we saw hidden costs when accounting for latency SLAs and retries. how do you model retries?
04:03 Marina: good point. we recommend bundling SLO buffers into the pilot — for retries we include an estimate; also our console shows token-level cost with retries and error rates so you can see realized unit economics.
04:20 Ethan: on dedicated vs hosted — dedicated reserves GPU pools; you pay commit + usage. unit costs drop because you control instance types and quantization profiles; plus you can pin model versions and use private KMS. but reserved capacity needs a commit and you need to estimate peak throughput to get right sizing.
04:44 Priya: what's the overhead for private? if we want VPC + customer-managed KMS and audit logs, what's the delta?
04:50 Marina: Private (VPC/on-prem) typically has a platform license and infra costs — higher initial fixed cost but similar per-token after you scale. for your QPS profile, private might make sense long-term but hosted or dedicated lower friction for pilot.
05:08 Daniel: for benchmarking, what specific configs should we test?
05:12 Ethan: propose three configurations: 1) Hosted baseline with default batching and caching, 2) Dedicated with reserved pool and aggressive batching but latency cap = 150ms p50, 3) Dedicated/private with KV caching enabled and quantized model. we'll run identical prompt sets and measure tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and cost per effective generated token.
05:38 Marina: i'll put numbers but example ballpark: hosted per-gen token might be $0.0008–0.0012 depending on model; dedicated can drop that to $0.0002–0.0005 with reserved commits — but these are illustrative. real delta depends on sequence length and cache hit rate.
06:00 Sanjay: those per-token numbers: is that only generation tokens or includes input encoder tokens?
06:05 Marina: includes billed compute for both, but caching reduces encoder billed compute. we'll show line-by-line in sheet.
06:12 Daniel: can you do a quick mental math: if we do 20k req/day * ~2.3k total tokens avg (in+out) that's ~46M tokens/month. pilot with 20k/month budget? sorry we said 20k dollars pilot —amm is that realistic?
06:28 Sanjay: yes $20k pilot budget month 1.
06:31 Marina: at 46M tokens, even at $0.0008 that's ~36.8k, so you'd need caching/batching to hit the $20k. that's why pilot is valuable to show realized unit economics.
06:46 Priya: what's the typical cache hit rate you see on customer benchmarks?
06:50 Ethan: varies a lot — for templated prompts we see 40-70% cache hit; for more open-ended queries it's lower. also you can do client-side prefix canonicalization to improve hit rates.
07:05 Daniel: about batching: you mentioned latency trade-off. can we set a latency SLO like p50<150ms and allow p95 to be higher? we care more about average throughput during peak.
07:14 Ethan: yes, Redwood routing supports SLOs per-route; you can set latency targets and the runtime adapts batching. you can also route high-priority traffic to low-latency nodes and cheaper traffic to high-batch nodes. that's a policy decision.
07:34 Priya: are there extra costs for tracing and logs? we need high fidelity for model outputs for audit.
07:40 Marina: observability is included but higher retention or advanced tracing is an add-on. we'll include options in the pricing sheet.
07:50 Daniel: any gotchas on quantization? we prefer 8-bit if it doesn't drop quality too much.
07:55 Ethan: quantization helps memory and throughput; for some models 8-bit is fine, for others you may see small quality differences. we can run A/B evals on your prompt set to measure ROUGE or other metrics tied to quality. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations.
08:15 Sanjay: procurement — what's the typical procurement lead time for dedicated or private?
08:20 Marina: hosted is immediate; dedicated usually 2–4 weeks to provision reserved capacity after contract; private can be 4–8 weeks depending on infra approvals. we'll provide a timeline in the follow-up.
08:32 Daniel: sample benchmark plan and config?
08:35 Ethan: we'll ask you to provide 1) prompt corpus (~2000 prompts representing distribution), 2) request sizes and concurrency targets, 3) target seeds for stability. we'll run 3 runs each config: cold start, steady-state, and peak bursts. we'll measure token throughput, end-to-end latency, GPU utilization, and cost per effective output token.
09:02 Priya: for private KMS integration — are there supported providers? we use AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault.
09:08 Marina: we support AWS KMS and several HSM providers; Vault is commonly integrated in private deployments. will share the docs.
09:18 Daniel: some transcribed bits — i heard "red word" in the transcript export. small thing.
09:22 Marina: yeah sometimes fireflies misfires.
09:25 Ethan: also note we meter at the token and GPU op level; the console will show top-of-route token breakdown so you can attribute cost to features.
09:34 Daniel: what about burst capacity? we have market open spikes. we need graceful degradation not errors.
09:39 Ethan: Redwood Dedicated has burst capacity options and automated fallback to hosted-compatible variants if capacity is constrained; routing policy can favor latency or cost. so in peak you can burst to hosted to preserve availability.
09:52 Sanjay: that helps. on pricing, for pilot we want firm caps and alerts.
09:58 Marina: we'll set a pilot cap and alerts in the contract and the console.
10:03 Daniel: any competitor differences we should be aware of? we looked at both OpenAI and Anthropic — both have simple pricing but less control over private deployments.
10:12 Marina: yes, Anthropic/OpenAI simpler but less flexible for private, and cost control levers like dedicated batch tuning are limited. Vertex AI has good infra options but stitching cross-cloud and vendor lock can be a concern. we'll highlight differences in the follow-up.
10:30 Priya: next — benchmarks schedule? we can start next monday.
10:34 Marina: sounds good. ethan will run benchmark plan and we'll provision a small hosted trial first.
10:40 Ethan: i'll share a bench checklist. also quick note on model selection: smaller distilled models with quantization often give best cost/perf; we'll recommend candidates based on your quality bar.
10:57 Daniel: quality bar — we need summaries to keep 95% of current human scoring. we'll include prompts for eval.
11:05 Marina: ok recap and actions: send pricing/cost model + SOC2 docs (Marina), bench plan and configs (Ethan), Northwind to provide prompt set and QPS goals (Priya/Daniel), CFO confirm budget/process (Sanjay). schedule bench next Monday.
11:26 Sanjay: sounds good, thanks everyone.
11:30 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: transcription contains typical mis-hearings, occasional speaker mislabels (fireflies). timestamps approximate every ~30-90s. The technical segment focused heavily on batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization and routing policies — all tied back to unit economics and pilot measurement.
